clue.text: I left German city as champ

indicators.note: I left means the letter I departs from the city name, so it is taken out

parts.note: Munich is the Bavarian capital

explanation.surface: Someone departs a German city as a champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I left' reads as a traveller's story, but it tells you to take I out of MUNICH. 'Champ' is the verb: to chew noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: To champ is to chew noisily, which is also what you do when you chomp loudly on food.

clue.text: Gets as much as possible from fish and drink

parts.words: Gets as much as possible from
parts.note: milks means exploits, wringing every last bit out of something
hake is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone getting all they can from fish and drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A milkshake is a drink of milk whisked with flavouring or ice cream.

clue.text: Unpleasant lot of leaders, except for the first two

indicators.note: except for the first two means the opening pair of letters is dropped

parts.note: a dynasty is a line of rulers from one family

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a crowd of bosses, sparing the top pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lot of leaders' looks like a group of bosses, but a dynasty is a family line of rulers; drop its first two letters, DY.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty and unpleasant both describe something disagreeable or offensive.

clue.text: Sybarite has done this wrong

indicators.note: wrong signals that the letters of done this are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A pleasure-seeker has committed some misdeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has' is linking; 'wrong' shuffles DONE THIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sybarite lives for luxury and pleasure, as a pleasure-seeker does.

clue.text: Potter concerned with jam primarily

indicators.note: primarily says the word for jam comes first, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: a jam, a tight spot, is a mess
concerned with means about, as in a book about cats

explanation.surface: A remark about a potter whose work is chiefly to do with jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter' looks like a noun (a maker of pots, or Harry), but it is the verb: to potter is to idle about. 'Primarily' puts MESS first.
explanation.definitionFit: To potter is to pass time doing small, aimless tasks, the same idle pottering as fooling around.

clue.text: A child could say

indicators.note: say signals the word is spoken, giving one with the same sound

parts.note: might means could, as in it might rain

explanation.surface: A remark on what a small youngster might come out with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could say' reads as a child speaking, but 'say' signals a word heard aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A mite is a small child, a tiny tot, the way one speaks fondly of a little one.

clue.text: Some fish float, we hear, on the sea surface — they're learning

parts.note: a school is a shoal of fish

indicators.note: we hear signals a word that sounds the same but is spelt differently

parts.note: a float marking a spot on the sea is a buoy

explanation.surface: A scene of fish and floats bobbing at the surface of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the sea surface' describes the floats, the buoys, whose sound gives BOYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils at school are learners, studying lessons in class.

clue.text: State to make enquiry into another…

indicators.note: into places the word for making an enquiry inside the other piece

parts.note: Ala is the abbreviation for Alabama, another US state
ask means make an enquiry

explanation.surface: A government begins an investigation into a further matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like the verb (to declare) but is a US state; 'another' is another state too.
explanation.definitionFit: Alaska is the largest US state, in the far north-west.

clue.text: … in difficulties immediately

definitions.meaning: in a tight corner, under pressure

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means both put in an awkward position and at once, without leaving the place.

clue.text: Grow up lacking love and spirit

indicators.note: lacking means the letter for love is missing from the word
up, in a down clue, means the word for grow is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to sprout is to grow
O is love, the zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: Someone matures without love and with little spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' turns SPROUT to TUORPS; 'lacking' removes the O. The answer is short for turpentine, white spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Turpentine is a solvent spirit, the oil used to thin paint.

clue.text: Where die-hards died, see, died in pain

parts.note: la is an old exclamation meaning look or see, like lo

indicators.note: in places the letter for died inside the word for pain

parts.note: a stitch is a sharp pain in the side
D is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A grim battlefield note: stubborn fighters perished in agony at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Died' appears in both halves: the definition alludes to soldiers fighting to the end, the wordplay uses its abbreviation. LA is a dated cry meaning 'see!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who refuse to give up resist to the very end, making a final stand in the final trench of a defence.

clue.text: Bill, a rising player

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill
a tor is a rocky hill, a rising of the ground

explanation.surface: A man named Bill is a player on the way up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name and 'rising' like a career, but AC is an account and a TOR is a hill on Dartmoor-type moorland.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is a performer on stage, someone who takes roles in a play.

clue.text: Saw the female influence in 29

indicators.note: in places the female principle inside the word that clue 29 gives

parts.note: clue 29 across is a word for flag or wilt, which sag also means
yin is the female, passive principle in Chinese philosophy

explanation.surface: A proverb on how women's influence works within another entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is the noun, an old proverb, not the tool or the verb. The 29 is a cross-reference to the 29-across answer, whose meaning (flag, wilt) supplies the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old maxim or proverb, a familiar adage repeated through generations.

clue.text: In favour of having guards permanently

parts.note: for means in favour of, as in voting for
keeps means guards or protects

explanation.surface: Someone backs having sentries stationed for good.
explanation.definitionFit: To have something for good is to own it permanently, with no return expected.

clue.text: Able to tire out and wipe out

indicators.note: out means the letters of the preceding words are set out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Something able to exhaust and destroy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' looks part of 'tire out', but it shuffles ABLE TO TIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate is to destroy completely, leaving no trace.

clue.text: Capital is involved in a bad, repeated blunder

indicators.note: blunder means the letters go wrong and are jumbled into a new order
repeated means the words a bad are used twice over

explanation.surface: Someone is caught up in an awful mistake, made twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeated' doubles A BAD to ABADABAD; 'blunder' shuffles that with IS. 'Involved in' is linking. The answer is the capital of Ethiopia.
explanation.definitionFit: Addis Ababa is the capital city of Ethiopia.

clue.text: Put out of countenance, girl's sweet

parts.note: Di's is the possessive of Di, a girl's name
a comfit is a sugar-coated sweet

explanation.surface: A girl's sweet embarrasses someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl's' looks like 'belonging to a girl', which it is: DI'S. A comfit is an old-fashioned sugared sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: To discomfit is to unsettle or embarrass, making someone lose composure.

clue.text: Hurried and saw one going

indicators.note: going means the letter for one leaves the word

parts.note: spied means saw, caught sight of
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone hurried off and noticed a person leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is past tense of see, SPIED; 'going' removes I (one).
explanation.definitionFit: Hurried and raced both describe moving fast, so a car that zoomed past did exactly this.

clue.text: Chapter I'd rewritten for peanuts

indicators.note: rewritten says the letters are written again in another order

explanation.surface: A writer reworked a chapter for a pittance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For peanuts' means very cheaply.
explanation.definitionFit: Peanuts means a trifling sum, so something bought this way costs next to nothing.

clue.text: Beloved, I would store up every date from the beginning

parts.note: I'd is short for I would

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means the word for store is read bottom to top

parts.note: a silo is a store for grain

indicators.note: from the beginning takes the opening letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A lover saves every date from the start of the relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' turns SILO into OLIS; E and D come from the starts of 'every date'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone worshipped or adored is beloved, held up as an object of devotion.

clue.text: A point in time, a stage

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words time, a stage, spanning the gap

explanation.surface: A definition of a moment: a point in time is a stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A point in time' looks like the definition, but only 'A point' defines: a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass point is one of the four cardinal directions, the one where the sun rises.

clue.text: "Do try it!" — ice-breaking journalist

indicators.note: breaking means the letters are broken up and rearranged together

explanation.surface: A newspaper writer urging a reluctant guest to break the ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ice-breaking' suggests social chat, but 'breaking' shuffles DO TRY IT together with ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A city editor is the newspaper journalist who runs the financial or local news desk.

clue.text: Crush is a drink

definitions.meaning: to quash or stamp out, as a rumour
whisky from north of the border

explanation.surface: A crush is described as a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch is to put an end to, as a rumour, and the word also names whisky distilled in Scotland.

clue.text: Brother was in pain — opened up

parts.note: ached means was in pain

explanation.surface: A brother in pain finally talked about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opened up' looks like confiding, but it means raised a subject, or pierced a cask.
explanation.definitionFit: To broach a topic is to raise it for discussion, as one also taps a barrel to open it.

clue.text: Start a job in oratory

indicators.note: in oratory means when spoken aloud in a speech, so the word is heard

parts.note: a berth is a job or post, as in a cushy berth

explanation.surface: Beginning a career as a public speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oratory' looks like a chapel or public speaking career; it signals speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A start is a beginning, and a baby's arrival is life's beginning.

clue.text: Priest gives class a name

parts.note: cl is the abbreviation for class
Eric is a man's name

explanation.surface: A clergyman gives his school form a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleric is a member of the clergy, such as a priest or minister.

clue.text: One liable to charge cash

definitions.meaning: a large horned animal apt to stampede at people

explanation.surface: Someone who may charge for money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' looks like billing; it is a charging beast. RHINO is dated British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal is famous for charging, and the slang word also means money.

clue.text: Bird making love in bed

indicators.note: in places the letter for love inside the word for bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
O is love, the zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A bird making love in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A coot is a black water bird with a white forehead.

clue.text: Judge taken to appeal and put right

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, judges a game
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A judge's decision goes to appeal and is corrected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appeal' sounds legal, but IT is sex appeal, as in 'the It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: To refit is to repair or re-equip, setting a ship or machine in working order again.

clue.text: Miserable existence led by Cerberus?

definitions.meaning: a wretched, put-upon way of living
Cerberus is the three-headed hound guarding the Greek underworld, so whatever life he led is a hound's

explanation.surface: Pity the guard dog of Hades, stuck with a wretched lot.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: a hound's life, taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a wretched, harried existence, while Cerberus is a hound and so lives one literally.

clue.text: One was late getting these bearings

definitions.text: One was late getting these bearings

parts.words: One was late getting these bearings
parts.note: the late here means dead, and the bearings are heraldic arms displayed on a diamond-shaped board at a dead person's house

explanation.surface: Someone who arrived late got their bearings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' looks like tardy and 'bearings' like direction, but late means deceased and bearings are heraldic.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatchment is a diamond-shaped panel bearing a dead person's coat of arms, hung on their house during mourning.

clue.text: Flag doesn't really offer operator protection when the leaders are taken

indicators.note: the leaders of the words are their opening letters, and only those are kept

explanation.surface: A complaint that an operator is left unprotected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' is the verb: to tire or wilt.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to tire or wilt, as a plant sags without water.
